svg.text: System trays on Linux — how they work today

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: the protocols as they are (2026-11): XEmbed, StatusNotifierItem, com.canonical.dbusmenu · generated by doc/diagrams/linux_system_tray.py

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: A tray icon is a small, lasting sign of a program in the panel: a chat with new messages, a cloud folder syncing, a game client running without a window. Linux has had two ways to do it. The old one lets the application put a window of its

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: own into the panel; it works only on X11. The one in use today, StatusNotifierItem, makes the application describe its icon over D-Bus and lets the panel draw it, the menu included: it works on Wayland, follows the theme and the scale, and a

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: panel can show it however it likes (in a bar, in a list, in a Control Center).

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: Three roles share the work: the item (the application's icon), the watcher (a registry, one per session) and the host (the panel that shows the icons). A session without a watcher has no tray: applications look for one at their start and do

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: something else when there is none (an X11 icon, a window, nothing at all).

svg.text: X11 only: Wayland has no such thing as one client's window inside another's. Under Wayland these icons work only for X11 programs (Xwayland), through a bridge (xembedsniproxy, below).

svg.text: The panel gets pixels it cannot restyle: no theme colours, blurry on a scaled screen, invisible on a dark panel; no tooltip or status it could read; nothing for screen readers.

svg.text: The application exports a D-Bus object that describes its icon: a name from the icon theme (or pixmaps), a tooltip, a status (passive, active, needs attention) and a menu. The panel reads it

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: and draws it its own way, and calls the application back when the user clicks.

svg.text: Works on Wayland and X11 alike; icons from the theme, sharp at any scale, light or dark as the panel needs; a status the panel can act on (hide passive icons, show those that need attention);

svg.text: the main actions and Quit: some panels never send Activate. Watch IsStatusNotifierHostRegistered and the host signals:

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: without a host, show your window instead of hiding where nobody can reach you. Accept the activation token.

svg.text: As a panel or a session

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: Start the watcher before the programs that autostart, or their first check finds none. Exactly one watcher: two processes

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: trying to own the name leave icons in the wrong one. Accept an object path where a bus name is expected (libappindicator,

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: some Electron versions do it). Drop items when their name goes. Read the icon by name first; draw the menu yourself.

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: Coalesce bursts of New… signals. Hand an activation token to Activate on Wayland.

svg.text: Nobody owns org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher (checked 2026-11-26): kded6 is started only on demand and its watcher module with

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: it, and Maia has no host. So icons do not appear, and programs that close to the tray cannot be brought back.

svg.text: A service of the session that owns the watcher name and is the one host (TODO.md item 4): it tracks the items, reads their

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: icons, tooltips and menus, and gives them to the frontends over Cap'n Proto, so that Lumen's taskbar and the Maia frontend

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: draw the same items their own way; clicks, scrolling and menu events go back through it, with an activation token. It starts

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: early in session.toml. kded6's statusnotifierwatcher module is switched off in Maia's kded6rc (as networkmanagement already

text.font-family: Noto Sans, DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: is), and xembedsniproxy starts with the session for X11 icons.
